collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager wants a ceremony to mark a fresh start after a hard time: create a new one, or adapt an old one.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has had a hard couple of years, and does not want to talk about why. But (subject.he/she) feels like (subject.he/she) is starting over, and wants to mark it somehow. There is no ceremony on Isola for that. (friend) knows a lot of old ceremonies, and thinks one of them might fit. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) makes up a ceremony of (subject.his/her) own: (subject.he/she) swims out to the rocks at dawn, leaves a stone there, and swims back. A few friends wait on the beach with a blanket. It means nothing to anyone else. It means everything to (subject).

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) suggests the old ceremony for a new canoe: washing it in the sea, painting it, and giving it a name. They do it for (subject) instead of a canoe, which is very silly and involves a lot of paint. (subject) laughs harder than (subject.he/she) has in a long time.
